claims.text: A NiCr matrix containing MoS2 can provide stable low-friction performance from room temperature to 800 °C.
Adding MoS2 to NiCr will retain the mechanical strength of the base alloy.
Hot pressing or spark plasma sintering of NiCr powder containing submicron MoS2 particulates will form a dense composite.
The proposed tribological performance applies under cyclic loading in an inert or low-oxygen environment.
MoS2 will be present as well-dispersed platelets within the NiCr matrix.
The dispersed MoS2 platelets will form a uniform lubricating tribofilm at high temperatures.
MoS2 platelets slide easily and thereby reduce friction.
A protective MoS2-containing tribofilm mitigates adhesive wear.
Mitigation of adhesive wear preserves the NiCr matrix at elevated temperatures.
The composite will sustain a friction coefficient of approximately 0.15 to 0.25 from room temperature to 800 °C.
The composite will show minimal deterioration in mechanical performance over the tested temperature range.
Conventional NiCr without MoS2 typically exhibits increased friction above approximately 400 °C.
Conventional NiCr without MoS2 typically exhibits increased wear above approximately 400 °C.
The elevated-temperature friction and wear of conventional NiCr arise from insufficient lubrication.
Prolonged exposure to highly oxidizing environments at elevated temperatures may reduce the lubrication efficacy of MoS2.
Prolonged exposure to wet environments at elevated temperatures may reduce the lubrication efficacy of MoS2.
Friction and wear improvements depend on MoS2 morphology.
Friction and wear improvements depend on composite processing conditions.
Friction and wear improvements depend on the testing environment.
